children: Brazil's budget proposal for next year will include a 6 billion reais ($1.2 billion) capital injection into state-run postal service Correios as part of a turnaround plan for the cash-strapped company, the government said on Sunday.

The funding is intended to provide Correios with "greater stability to continue negotiating with clients and suppliers" as it implements its restructuring plan and seeks to restore profitability, according to a statement.

Signed by Management Minister Esther Dweck, Planning Minister Bruno Moretti and Communications Minister Frederico Siqueira Filho, the statement added that liquidity support had enabled Correios to improve operations and strengthen its debt profile.
The 2027 budget bill will be submitted to Congress on Monday.
Correios reported a second-quarter net loss of 2.4 billion reais on Saturday, narrowing 5.5% from a year earlier.

President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who is seeking re-election in October, has recently said the government intends to rehabilitate rather than privatize Correios, which has reported losses for several consecutive quarters.
The company approved a restructuring plan last year to bolster short-term liquidity and has already completed 12 billion reais in federally guaranteed credit operations.
Correios said on Saturday it is also in advanced talks for a new credit operation worth roughly 7 billion reais, also backed by the federal government.

The company cited falling revenue from traditional postal services, rising operating costs, legacy legal liabilities, intensifying competition in logistics and the costs of maintaining a nationwide universal postal network among the challenges weighing on its results.
